designSummary: Comparison of two consecutive annual groups of trial episodes; costs per episode summarised by mean with bootstrap intervals; consequences as proportions with exact intervals.
sampleSize: The sample is fixed by activity: about 88 episodes a year gives about 176. With a standard deviation of episode cost of about 110 (a planning value from the spread of contact costs; the observed value replaces it), the 95 percent confidence interval for the difference in mean cost has a half-width of about 33 (110 times the square root of 2/88, times 1.96). The expected saving of about 43 per episode (one nurse clinic slot at 64 less one call at 21, claim c3) would therefore be distinguishable from zero if it holds. Unplanned attendances near 11 percent give a half-width of about 9 percentage points for the difference, so consequences are described, not tested.
primaryAnalysis: Difference in mean health service cost per episode (2027 minus 2026) with a 95 percent bias-corrected bootstrap interval from 2,000 resamples. Costs in 2026 prices; no discounting within a trial week.
secondaryAnalysis: The same analysis for patient and companion costs and for the two perspectives combined; proportions with exact intervals for on-time implant decisions, unplanned attendances and infections; deterministic sensitivity analyses varying nurse time per call by half and double, the same-day review rate, the per-kilometre rate and the proportion of companions losing a working day; restriction to single-lead trials.
missingData: Missing resource items are counted as missing, never as zero; episodes with missing emergency department linkage are reported and analysed in a sensitivity analysis that assumes the 2026 attendance rate.
multiplicity: One primary comparison; everything else is presented as a cost-consequence table with intervals and no significance claims.
software: R with the boot package; costing spreadsheet and analysis script archived before the 2027 data are opened.
overfittingGuards: Resource list and unit costs fixed before analysis
No adjustment model beyond the pre-specified single-lead restriction
summary: About 176 episodes give a half-width of about 33 for the cost difference; consequences are reported descriptively with intervals.
